title: Sokołowski's Conjecture (Polynomial Neighborhood Complexity of Planar Graphs)
statement_text: There exists a constant $c$ such that $|\{N^{r}[v]\cap A\mid v\in V(G)\}|=\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(r^{c}|A|)$ for every planar graph $G$, every nonempty subset $A$ of vertices, and every nonnegative integer $r$.
context_text: Sokołowski conjectured that the neighborhood complexity of planar graphs is polynomial, following his earlier result showing a bound of $\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(r^{7}|A|^{3})$, which achieved polynomial dependence on $r$ at the cost of a cubic dependence on $|A|$. The general bound given by Reidl, Sánchez Villaamil and Stravopoulos is exponential, so a polynomial bound for specific classes would be a significant improvement.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture in full: the neighborhood complexity of planar graphs is in $\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(r^{4})$, and moreover the strictly stronger profile complexity of planar graphs (and all proper minor-closed classes) is also in $\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(r^{4})$.
notes: Abstract cites the conjecture as 'Sokołowski (2021)'; the bibliography entry [28] lists the published version as Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, 30(2):P2.3, 2023, suggesting the conjecture appeared in an earlier preprint.

title: Problem 41
statement_text: Determine the profile and neighborhood complexities of planar graphs up to a constant factor. For profile complexity, it is known to be in $\Omega(r^{3})$ and in $\mathcal{O}(r^{4})$. For neighborhood complexity, it is known to be in $\Omega(r^{2})$ and in $\mathcal{O}(r^{4})$.
context_text: For a vertex $v$ of $G$, $N^r[v]$ is the ball of radius $r$ around $v$ (vertices at distance at most $r$). The neighborhood complexity of a graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is the minimum function $f$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{C}$, every non-empty $A\subseteq V(G)$ and every integer $r\ge0$, $|\{N^r[v]\cap A: v\in V(G)\}|\le f(r)|A|$ (for subgraph-closed classes, its existence characterizes bounded expansion). The profile of a vertex $u$ on $A$ at distance $r$ is the $|A|$-tuple of distances $\mathrm{dist}(u,a)$, $a\in A$, with values larger than $r$ replaced by $+\infty$; the profile complexity of $\mathcal{C}$ is the minimum $f$ such that the number of distinct profiles on $A$ at distance $r$ is at most $f(r)|A|$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, non-empty $A$ and $r$. Profile complexity is an upper bound on neighborhood complexity. Sokołowski proved the bound $|\{N^r[v]\cap A\}|=\mathcal{O}(r^7|A|^3)$ for planar graphs and conjectured that their neighborhood complexity is polynomial in $r$. The authors prove this: the profile (hence neighborhood) complexity of planar graphs is $\mathcal{O}(r^4)$, and they construct planar graphs (of bounded treewidth) showing that the profile complexity is $\Omega(r^3)$, which yields an $\Omega(r^2)$ lower bound for neighborhood complexity. They also show that $K_t$-minor-free graphs have profile complexity $\mathcal{O}_t(r^{t^2-1})$ and graphs of Euler genus $g$ have profile complexity $\mathcal{O}_g(r^5)$, whereas $1$-planar graphs do not have polynomial neighborhood complexity.

title: Problem 42
statement_text: Are the profile and neighborhood complexities of $K_{t}$-minor-free graphs in $r^{\operatorname{\mathcal{O}}(t)}$?
context_text: For a vertex $v$ of $G$, $N^r[v]$ is the ball of radius $r$ around $v$ (vertices at distance at most $r$). The neighborhood complexity of a graph class $\mathcal{C}$ is the minimum function $f$ such that for every $G\in\mathcal{C}$, every non-empty $A\subseteq V(G)$ and every integer $r\ge0$, $|\{N^r[v]\cap A: v\in V(G)\}|\le f(r)|A|$ (for subgraph-closed classes, its existence characterizes bounded expansion). The profile of a vertex $u$ on $A$ at distance $r$ is the $|A|$-tuple of distances $\mathrm{dist}(u,a)$, $a\in A$, with values larger than $r$ replaced by $+\infty$; the profile complexity of $\mathcal{C}$ is the minimum $f$ such that the number of distinct profiles on $A$ at distance $r$ is at most $f(r)|A|$ for all $G\in\mathcal{C}$, non-empty $A$ and $r$. Profile complexity is an upper bound on neighborhood complexity. The authors prove that for every $t\ge1$ the profile complexity (hence the neighborhood complexity) of $K_t$-minor-free graphs is $\mathcal{O}_t(r^{t^2-1})$, so every proper minor-closed class has polynomial neighborhood complexity; for planar graphs they get $\mathcal{O}(r^4)$. The question asks whether the exponent of $r$ can be made linear in $t$ instead of quadratic.
